children: The iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF (IGV, Financials) has gained 24.5% over the past five weeks and is flashing a rare technical momentum signal that's only come up three other times in the ETF's history, All Star Charts notes.

The most recent five-week rate of change was 24.5%. IGV recently traded near $109.50. All Star Charts research director Alfonso De Pablos posted a graphic showing similar Thrust signs in 2002, 2009 and 2020.

All past signals were after a large drop and followed by a steady move up. This time, that does not promise the same result, but it does provide investors another reason to follow software companies after a steep 2026 rally.
The ETF's top holdings include Palantir at 10.29%, Palo Alto Networks at 9.72% and Microsoft at 9.18%. Some of its largest holdings are CrowdStrike, Salesforce and Oracle.
That matters given software has been on the rebound recently, having spent some of the year under pressure from valuation worries and evolving views on AI.
The main question now is whether the five-week spike of 24.5% is the beginning of another prolonged advance in software or just an extraordinarily rapid comeback.

title: Software Stocks Just Did Something They've Done Only Three Times Before
